body.id: Huruf Jepang pertama kita: hiragana. Satu huruf, satu bunyi.
body.en: Our first Japanese letters: hiragana. One letter, one sound.

body.id: あ い う え お dibaca a i u e o. え selalu é, seperti di sate.
body.en: あ い う え お say a i u e o, just like in Indonesian.

body.id: Halo = こんにちは (konnichiwa). Terima kasih = ありがとう (arigatō, ō dibaca panjang).
body.en: Hello = こんにちは (konnichiwa). Thank you = ありがとう (arigatō, say the ō long).

items.source: Digital Daijisen dictionary (Shogakukan), entry 'konnichiwa': the greeting is short for 'konnichi wa…' ('as for today…') with the rest of the sentence left off; read via kotobank.jp.

model_answer.id: Di こんにちは, huruf terakhir は dibaca wa, bukan ha. Dulu salam ini kalimat panjang yang dimulai "konnichi wa…" ("hari ini…"). Ujung kalimatnya hilang, salamnya tetap!
model_answer.en: In こんにちは, the last letter は is read wa, not ha. It began as a longer sentence starting "konnichi wa…" ("today…"). The end of the sentence dropped off, but the greeting stayed!

items.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'kana' (britannica.com/topic/kana): hiragana developed from cursive forms of kanji; Christopher Seeley, A History of Writing in Japan (Brill, 1991).

model_answer.id: Dulu orang Jepang menulis dengan kanji dari Tiongkok. Kanji yang ditulis cepat-cepat jadi melengkung, lalu lama-lama menjadi hiragana. Huruf あ dulunya sebuah kanji!
model_answer.en: Long ago, Japanese was written with kanji from China. Kanji written very fast became curvy and, over time, turned into hiragana. The letter あ was once a kanji!
